headline: Margin expansion and lower funding costs lift profit
summary_short: Cullen/Frost's Q2 2026 revenue was $576M (+5.3% y/y, +0.2% q/q) and net income rose to $172M (+9.6% y/y), with diluted EPS of $2.70 up 13.0% y/y as net interest margin expanded to 3.75% on lower deposit and repo funding costs.
summary_long: Net interest income and margin expansion (taxable-equivalent NIM +8bp y/y to 3.75%) drove the profit gain, aided by lower average costs on interest-bearing deposits and repurchase agreements plus loan and tax-exempt-securities growth, partly offset by lower loan yields. Non-interest income rose 11.8% y/y on higher trust/investment-management fees, deposit service charges, and card fees; non-interest expense rose 3.7% y/y on salaries, benefits, and technology costs. Credit loss expense fell to $9.8M from $13.1M as net charge-offs eased to an annualized 0.17% of average loans. CET1 stood at 13.95%, comfortably above well-capitalized minimums. Shareholders' equity grew to $4.6B on retained earnings, though total cash fell $677M q/q on deployment into loans and securities. No forward guidance was disclosed in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Net income available to common rose on an $18.1M increase in net interest income, an $11.0M increase in non-interest income, and a $3.4M decrease in credit loss expense, partly offset by a $14.6M rise in non-interest expense and higher income tax expense.

Net interest income rose on NIM expansion (lower deposit/repo funding costs, higher loan and tax-exempt-securities volumes) and non-interest income grew on trust/investment fees and deposit service charges.
Higher pretax income drove the gain; the effective tax rate was flat at 15.9% y/y for the quarter, so none of the increase came from a tax-rate change.
Net income growth plus a smaller diluted share count (62.45M vs 64.35M a year earlier) from ongoing treasury-stock purchases funded the larger EPS gain.
Cash held in the Federal Reserve interest-bearing account was deployed into loan growth (+$1.1B YTD) and securities purchases per the investing-activities cash flow section.
Equity grew on $343.0M of six-month net income and $10.6M of stock-based compensation, partly offset by $163.2M of treasury purchases, $132.1M of dividends, and an $8.7M AOCI loss.
